pages.text: This is the transmitter from lesson 2, `S(p) = 0.16p + 4`. Its shadow straight down on the input axis, 0% to 100%, is its [[domain]], and its shadow straight across on the output axis, 4 to 20 mA, is its [[range]]. Drag either end of the line and both shadows change.

pages.name: A hump
pages.task: This hump's top sits on the line `x = 0`, at a height of 6. What is its domain?
pages.why: The hump's shadow straight down runs from its left end at −4 to its right end at 4, so its domain is −4 to 4. The 6 where it meets the line `x = 0` is a height, an output.

pages.name: The one-over
pages.text: This is the one-over, `y = 1/x`. At 0 the beam finds no value, because no number times 0 gives 1, so the input shadow has a hole at 0, and an input where a rule divides by zero like this is called a [[pole]]. The output shadow has a hole at 0 for its own reason: 1 divided by any number is never 0.

pages.name: A narrower level
pages.task: A tank's level only ever runs from 25% to 75%. What range does the transmitter give?
pages.why: Put the domain's ends through the rule. `S(25) = 0.16 × 25 + 4 = 8` and `S(75) = 0.16 × 75 + 4 = 16`, and the line climbs steadily between, so the range is 8 to 16 mA.

pages.task: Now the square's inputs are set from −2 to 3. What is its range?
pages.why: The ends give `(−2)² = 4` and `3² = 9`, but the U dips to 0 at `x = 0` on the way, so the range is 0 to 9, not 4 to 9.

pages.alt: A graph of y equals x squared, input along the bottom, output up the side. The shadow on the input axis runs from minus 2 to 3. The shadow on the output axis runs from 0 to 9.

pages.name: The flow meter
pages.text: The flow meter's rule is the square root, with pressure difference and flow as fractions of full, so both shadows run 0 to 1. But the outputs bunch towards the top: half the pressure difference already gives 0.707 of the flow, because `√0.5 = 0.707`. Tap the tabs to compare every graph's shadows.

pages.name: A 12 V supply
pages.task: A 12 V supply feeds a resistance set from 3 to 12 Ω, so `I = 12/R`. What range of current flows?
pages.why: At 3 Ω the current is `12 ÷ 3 = 4` A, and at 12 Ω it is `12 ÷ 12 = 1` A. The curve falls steadily between them, so the range is 1 to 4 A, its ends coming from the domain's ends the other way round.

pages.name: Two machines
pages.task: Which input does `y = 1/x` take but `y = √x` refuse?
pages.why: `1 ÷ −4 = −0.25`, so the one-over takes −4, but no ordinary number times itself gives −4, so the root refuses it. The one-over refuses only 0.
pages.alt: Two graphs side by side, y equals 1 over x and y equals the square root of x. The shadow on the input axis of y equals 1 over x runs over every number but 0. The shadow on the input axis of y equals the square root of x runs from 0 and on up. The beam up from minus 4 on y equals 1 over x reads minus 0.25. The beam up from minus 4 on y equals the square root of x finds no value.
